summary: This article explains why the Asir mountains in southwestern Saudi Arabia are cool, rainy, and green, and how their forests, terraces, wildlife, and traditions make the region special.
introduce: Draw a simple cause → effect arrow on the board and ask students for an everyday example, such as “I did not sleep, so I felt tired.” Tell them that while reading “The Green Mountains of Asir” they will find at least two cause-and-effect links.

keyTerms.def: a large area of a country or the world
how high a place is above the level of the sea
a small amount of water in the air or in something

challengeTerms.def: the height of a place above sea level
to change from a gas into a liquid, usually by cooling
all the living things in an area and the way they depend on each other and their surroundings

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that mountains are better places to live than flat lands? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain why Asir is greener than most of Saudi Arabia.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review region, altitude, and moisture, and let weak readers match cause cards to effect cards from the article with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use elevation, condense, and ecosystem in a short paragraph that explains one important cause-and-effect chain from the article.
